current_row.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 16:51 opens with no formula device, וְשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן כַּחֲצִ֥י חַטֹּאתַ֖יִךְ לֹ֣א חָטָ֑אָה וַתַּרְבִּ֤י אֶת תּוֹעֲבוֹתַ֨יִךְ֙ מֵהֵ֔נָּה וַתְּצַדְּקִי֙ אֶת אחותך בְּכָל תּוֹעֲבוֹתַ֖יִךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עשיתי (oshb:Ezek.16.51), continuing the comparative indictment by default: 'and Samaria did not commit half your sins.' Close side: the row ends at 16:58, the whole verse אֶת זִמָּתֵ֥ךְ וְאֶת תּוֹעֲבוֹתַ֖יִךְ אַ֣תְּ נְשָׂאתִ֑ים נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.16.58) ('you bear the penalty of your lewdness and your abominations, declares YHWH'), a verse-final variant close matched by a samekh recorded on this same verse. Two doubled/tripled Ketiv/Qere notes fall inside this span. MT 16:51 reads the ketivs אחותך and עשיתי, with the Qere layer giving אֲחוֹתַ֔יִךְ and עָשִֽׂית. MT 16:53 carries three notes on one verse -- the densest K/Q verse in this part -- reading the ketivs שבית (twice, once before 'Sodom' and once before 'Samaria') and ושבית, against the Qere readings שְׁב֤וּת, שְׁב֥וּת and וּשְׁב֥וּת (all forms of 'fortunes/captivity'). An editorial note also falls at 16:54 inside this span, disclosed as a single-witness vowel-reading divergence, not a text-critical claim about the row's content.

current_row.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 16:59 opens with the messenger formula כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.16.59) ('for thus says the Lord YHWH'), turning from the sisters comparison to YHWH's own covenant memory; the running text reads the ketiv ועשית in place of the pointed form here. Close side: the row runs to the chapter's own end, MT 16:63, the whole verse לְמַ֤עַן תִּזְכְּרִי֙ וָבֹ֔שְׁתְּ וְלֹ֨א יִֽהְיֶה לָּ֥ךְ עוֹד֙ פִּתְח֣וֹן פֶּ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י כְּלִמָּתֵ֑ךְ בְּכַפְּרִי לָךְ֙ לְכָל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔ית נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.16.63), whose final words are the utterance formula, matched by a samekh recorded on this same verse -- the strongest close available in the chapter, mark, refrain and chapter-end all coinciding. Inside the row, MT 16:62 closes with the second-person recognition formula, the whole verse וַהֲקִימוֹתִ֥י אֲנִ֛י אֶת בְּרִיתִ֖י אִתָּ֑ךְ וְיָדַ֖עַתְּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.16.62) ('and you shall know that I am YHWH'), a genuine refrain close that is nonetheless not treated as the row's own end, since 16:63 both continues the same covenant sentence grammatically and carries the stronger, mark-corroborated close.

current_row.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 19:1 opens with the distinct qinah-command onset וְאַתָּה֙ שָׂ֣א קִינָ֔ה אֶל נְשִׂיאֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.19.1) ('and you, take up a lamentation for the princes of Israel') -- not a word-event formula and not a son-of-man address, but the genre-naming command proper to a lament. Close side: the row runs to the chapter's own colophon, MT 19:14, the whole verse וַתֵּצֵ֨א אֵ֜שׁ מִמַּטֵּ֤ה בַדֶּ֨יהָ֙ פִּרְיָ֣הּ אָכָ֔לָה וְלֹא הָ֥יָה בָ֛הּ מַטֵּה עֹ֖ז שֵׁ֣בֶט לִמְשׁ֑וֹל קִ֥ינָה הִ֖יא וַתְּהִ֥י לְקִינָֽה (oshb:Ezek.19.14), whose last clause names its own genre a second time ('this is a lamentation, and it is used as a lamentation'), matched by a pe recorded on this same verse. A pe also falls mid-chapter, on 19:9, at the close of the lion-cubs figure -- לְמַ֗עַן לֹא יִשָּׁמַ֥ע קוֹל֛וֹ ע֖וֹד אֶל הָרֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.19.9) ('so that his voice should no more be heard on the mountains of Israel') -- immediately before the second figure opens at 19:10, אִמְּךָ֥ כַגֶּ֛פֶן בְּדָמְךָ֖ עַל מַ֣יִם שְׁתוּלָ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.19.10) ('your mother was like a vine in your vineyard, planted by the water'). That internal mark is disclosed and weighed, not adopted as a row seam: the colophon at 19:14 names the whole composition, both figures together, a single lamentation, so the span is kept as one row rather than split at its own internal parashah break.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Ezek.19.1 (disclosure: qinah-command onset, naming the genre directly)
oshb:Ezek.19.9 (disclosure: parashah: pe recorded on this verse, marking the internal seam between the lion figure and the vine figure; weighed and not taken as a row seam, single-witness)

oshb:Ezek.19.14 (disclosure: parashah: pe recorded on this verse, coinciding with the chapter's own colophon naming it a lamentation twice over; this verse also closes the surrounding undated-oracle collection, single-witness)
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting MT 19 at its internal pe (19:1-9 the lion cubs against 19:10-14 the vine) was weighed and not taken: the closing colophon at 19:14 explicitly names the whole fourteen-verse composition a single lamentation, and a qinah-labelled unit is kept whole on that ground.
current_row.literature_type_guess: qinah (lament) over the princes of Israel, cast in two figures: lion cubs, then a transplanted vine
